images.initialPrompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one polished landscape game UX concept painting for Sabobatage, 16:10 composition, full-bleed game screen, not device mockup and not website. Art direction: Boba Mischief, tactile cream paper cards with chunky espresso ink and pastel gouache cute boba ingredient characters. Scene: seated at a neighborhood bubble-tea shop's warm walnut and pale mint terrazzo counter, evening peach light, small shelves and tea jars at extreme edges, playable central counter calm and uncluttered. Render actual portrait playing cards at 63:88 proportions, warm cream frames, pastel header strips, cute tea cup, milk carton, pearls and peach character art. Visually rich crafted digital tabletop comparable to a premium boardgame videogame, with clean readable restrained typography. Layout: 3 opponent name coasters along far edge, each small concealed common card backs and completed-drink count. Central counter contains current player's SEVEN drink positions in one row: 4 occupied small overlapping ingredient stacks, then 3 unobtrusive cup-ring empty markers; each drink is a group of cards, NOT an illustrated cup replacing cards. One ingredient in hand is lifted, a compatible drink stack subtly rim-lit, dotted curved gesture path connecting them. Shared draw stack at middle-left, face-up discard at middle-right. Bottom foreground: beautiful fan of SEVEN actual portrait hand cards, large enough to see expressive art and titles, discrete exposed title tabs. Small paper order ticket immediately above hand says 'Your turn · 2 plays left'. Small brass arrow Undo token lower-left and small 'End turn' receipt tab lower-right. NO website header/footer, navigation bar, grid of boxed player panels, wide instruction banner, modal dialog, dashboard metrics, giant CTA. One understated shop wordmark in set dressing only, keep composition game-first. Actual text can be minimal: 'Peach Please', 'Taro Trouble', 'Your turn', '2 plays left', 'Undo', 'End turn'. Painted background depth but sharp card edges and UI labels; illustration style cohesive warm whimsical flat gouache, not photorealistic food. This is a new design-review concept painting, not an implemented screenshot. All card rules remain represented by subtle line typography, no long fake rules.

images.initialPrompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create a polished PORTRAIT 9:19.5 concept painting of a fullscreen mobile Sabobatage card-game screen, no physical phone bezel. Theme Boba Mischief: neighborhood boba shop counter, pale mint terrazzo, warm wood, espresso ink, cream paper cards with pastel gouache cute tea/milk/pearl characters. Real portrait cards 63:88, expressive illustrated art, crisp readable minimal UI. Make a native-feeling premium tabletop videogame, never a dashboard or website. Entire design fits a single phone screen with no page scrolling. Top 12%: three compact opponent coasters labelled 'Taro', 'Peach', 'Milk', each with tiny public drink count and hidden-hand count, no opponent hand faces. Center 43%: one focused drink composed of overlapping actual portrait tea and milk cards, with room for a topping. It belongs to 'Your counter', has a subtle green valid-placement rim. Below it a horizontal row of seven small numbered coaster selectors 1 through 7, one selected; completed coasters carry small check marks. Left edge small common-back draw pile; right edge small face-up discard pile; tiny journal receipt edge tab. Bottom 38%: the owner's hand is the dominant beautiful object, a fan of 7 portrait illustrated cards with legible exposed title tabs, one cute Boba card lifted bigger in center with a readable separate cream rule slip 'Draw one or play one extra'. A short two-option choice beneath the raised card reads 'Draw 1' and '+1 play', draw selected. The player taps the highlighted drink to place the card. Small contextual line 'Place Boba in a drink'. Bottom reachable edge: 'Undo' curved arrow, three pearl turn pips with two lit, 'End turn' folded receipt tab. Short labels and icons, generous finger-space. No giant top heading, no navbar/footer, no panels/cards containing forms, no modal, no confirmation, no long explanatory paragraphs, no internet or sync jargon. Cohesive gentle espresso lines, peach pink and matcha accents, restrained texture in the background only. Design review concept, not implemented screenshot.

images.initialPrompt: Use case: ui-mockup. Create one beautifully composed WIDE landscape 16:9 fullscreen SHARED TOUCH TABLE game concept painting for Sabobatage. Top-down flat camera, crafted tabletop videogame, warm cream-and-mint terrazzo boba-shop table with walnut edge and subtle bubble tea shop decor OUTSIDE card play areas. Boba Mischief art: espresso ink outlines, pastel gouache illustration, cute milk cartons, tea cups, tapioca pearls on cream portrait cards (63:88). FOUR occupied shops sit at north east south west edges, each faces outward toward its physical player: north cards upside-down, east cards rotated 90deg, west cards rotated -90deg, south cards upright. Each shop has SEVEN understated coaster drink positions in a shallow 4+3 arrangement (not boxed panels); some occupied by overlapping ingredient cards, empty positions small cup-rings. Shop name and 2/5 drinks on its own edge coaster. A small common card-back stack and hand COUNT at every seat; ABSOLUTELY NO FACE-UP PRIVATE HAND FANS anywhere on this public table. All face-up cards are clearly inside played drink groups. Center shared deck with common backs and faceup discard pile; quiet open central space with a faceup Sabobatage action card, cute masked tapioca pearl art. EXACTLY FIVE individual played ingredient cards across different shops have numbered cranberry selection rings 1,2,3,4,5; not whole-drink outlines. Small central printed ticket says 'Five targets chosen' and 'Reactions on your phones'. At each edge a small reaction state token 'Ready' or 'Thinking', oriented toward that seat. Clear ownership and stable physical seats, source-to-target fine threads across tabletop, restrained motion glow, strong spatial legibility. No website headers, no toolbar across top, no scrolling rows of boxed player dashboards, no modal, no prominent phone bezel, no game controls revealing private cards. Cozy tea-shop materials meet tactile premium card-game clarity. This is a design-review concept of a shared tabletop: the public cards are readable objects and players keep all hand faces on phones. Text incidental except central message. Don't mimic Greek Pantheon imagery; adopt its immersive game-world composition.
